market_context: United States/international; cooked fish and drained canned fish
title: Highest-Protein Fish: Ranking Per 100 Grams

seo.title: Highest-Protein Fish per 100 Grams
seo.meta_description: Compare tuna, sardines, cod, salmon, mackerel and lean white fish by protein per 100 grams, with context on omega-3 and mercury.
seo.search_intent: Rank fish by protein density while preserving broader nutrition context.

excerpt: Tuna is among the most protein-dense fish, but sardines, cod, salmon and mackerel are all close enough that omega-3, mercury and preparation often matter more than a few grams of protein.
content_html:
Most fish are already high-protein foods. A ranking can show concentration, but the spread is narrow enough that choosing fish solely because it has 25 instead of 22 grams of protein misses important differences in fat, omega-3s and mercury.

Representative protein ranking

FishApprox. protein/100 g
Water-packed tuna, drained24–26 g
Cooked tuna24–29 g
Sardines24–25 g
Cooked cod22–24 g
Cooked salmon22–25 g
Cooked mackerel22–24 g
Lean white fish such as pollock19–23 g

Tuna

Tuna is extremely protein-dense, especially drained canned tuna in water. Species matters for mercury: larger tuna species generally accumulate more than smaller “light” tuna species.

Sardines

Sardines combine high protein with EPA/DHA omega-3. Canned sardines with edible bones also deliver substantial calcium, making them nutritionally distinctive despite not always taking first place in protein.

Cod and lean white fish

Cod, haddock and pollock are lean, low-calorie protein sources. Salted cod is a different food from fresh cod because sodium is dramatically higher.

Salmon and mackerel

They contain more fat and calories than lean white fish, but much of the nutritional interest lies in long-chain omega-3 fats. A protein-per-calorie ranking would therefore place them lower without making them less nutritious overall.

Mercury changes how “best” should be defined

FDA/EPA fish advice groups species by mercury and recommends particular choices for people who are or might become pregnant and for children. Protein density should not override those species-specific recommendations.

Canned in oil versus water

Oil adds fat and calories, not protein. Drain canned fish consistently when comparing labels or database values.

Frequently asked questions

Which fish has the most protein?

Tuna is commonly near the top, but sardines, cod, salmon and mackerel are all protein-dense.

Does fatty fish contain less protein?

Not necessarily. Salmon remains high in protein; it simply carries more energy from fat.

Should I eat tuna every day for protein?

Variety is preferable, particularly because mercury levels differ among fish species.

faq.question: Which fish is highest in protein?
faq.answer: Tuna commonly ranks near the top at roughly 24–29 g per 100 g depending on species and preparation.

faq.question: Is salmon still high in protein?
faq.answer: Yes. Cooked salmon often provides roughly 22–25 g per 100 g while also supplying omega-3 fats.

faq.question: Why vary fish species?
faq.answer: Species differ in omega-3 content, mercury and other nutrients, so the highest protein number is not the only consideration.
